version.changelog:
cargo-analytics 1.4.1

- Updated install guidance to reference a shared prerequisites document, improving clarity.
- Changed the CLI install metadata to always fetch the latest version of @cargo-ai/cli.
- Minor documentation refinements for clarity and accuracy (no behavioral changes to skill functionality).

llm.summary: The skill is mostly a transparent Cargo analytics/export guide, but it also includes an under-warned command that can re-run workflow records and trigger real workspace side effects.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is analytics, downloading results, and exporting segment data, but the instructions also document `cargo-ai orchestration batch create` to re-run failed records; that is a state-changing execution action that can consume credits or trigger workflow effects.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Download/export commands are clearly part of the purpose, but broad full-run, full-segment, signed-URL, and email-filtered exports are presented with limited data-handling guardrails; the re-run step lacks an explicit confirmation or side-effect warning.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is disclosed as a Node package install of `@cargo-ai/cli@latest` with the `cargo-ai` binary; using `latest` is transparent but less reproducible than a pinned CLI version.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires a Cargo account and OAuth/API token access, which is proportionate for querying and exporting Cargo workspace data but means commands may access sensitive business or personal records.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No background workers, hidden persistence, privilege escalation, local indexing, or destructive local file operations were found in the markdown-only artifacts; credential persistence is limited to the referenced Cargo CLI login flow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only for users who are authorized to access and export Cargo workspace data. Treat downloaded files and signed URLs as sensitive, scope exports with workflow/date/status/model filters, and require explicit approval before using the documented failed-record re-run command because it can execute workflows and create side effects.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: the artifact includes a `batch create` re-run instruction inside an analytics/download skill, and it is not clearly separated as a mutating operation requiring explicit user approval.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly accepted: result downloads and signed URLs are expected for this skill, but the artifact under-warns that exported outputs and signed URLs can contain sensitive workspace data.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly accepted: segment export examples are purpose-aligned, but full exports and email-based filtering normalize broad personal-data extraction without authorization, minimization, storage, or retention guidance.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted as a lower-risk documentation gap: downloading error runs for debugging is expected, but the example does not warn that error artifacts may contain sensitive inputs, outputs, logs, or personal data.
